items.title: JWST detects water ice clouds on Jupiter-like exoplanet

featured_image.name: Webb Telescope directly images exoplanet Epsilon Indi Ab ...

items.description: Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope have detected evidence of water ice clouds in the atmosphere of Epsilon Indi Ab, a massive gas giant just 12 light-years from Earth, according to findings published in the Astrophysical Journal Letters. The discovery challenges widely used exoplanet atmosphere models, most of which do not account for clouds, and marks a step forward in the techniques scientists will eventually need to characterize Earth-like worlds.[1][2]

items.title: OpenAI plans $1.5B investment in PE joint venture

featured_image.name: OpenAI courts private equity to join enterprise AI venture

items.description:
OpenAI is set to commit up to $1.5 billion to a new joint venture with private equity firms as it races to embed its artificial intelligence tools across corporate America, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday.[1][2]

The AI company plans to invest an initial $500 million of its own equity into the venture, internally codenamed "DeployCo," with an option to invest an additional $1 billion at a later stage. The joint venture is expected to be valued at $10 billion as part of a funding round projected to close in early May.[3][4][5][6]

items.title: Crude dips as Trump extends Iran ceasefire unilaterally

featured_image.name: Trump says he will extend Iran ceasefire until negotiations ...

items.description: The ongoing war between the United States, Israel, and Iran has sent ripples through India's energy economy, pushing commercial LPG prices sharply higher and placing mounting pressure on the country's fuel supply chains, even as the government absorbs billions in lost revenue to keep retail petrol and diesel prices stable.

items.title: Pope Leo XIV reaches Equatorial Guinea as Africa tour nears end

featured_image.name: EGUINEA-VATICAN-DIPLOMACY-POPE

items.description: Pope Leo XIV called on young people in Cameroon to resist the temptation to migrate abroad, urging them instead to stay and work toward improving their communities, during a Mass attended by more than 120,000 people at Japoma Stadium in Douala on April 17.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump extends Iran ceasefire at Pakistan's request

featured_image.name: Iran war live: Trump extends ceasefire as Pakistan talks in disarray

items.description:
President Donald Trump announced Tuesday that the United States would extend its ceasefire with Iran indefinitely, reversing course just hours before the two-week truce was set to expire and after repeatedly saying an extension was "highly unlikely."

In a post on Truth Social, Trump cited a "seriously fractured" Iranian government and a direct appeal from Pakistan's Field Marshal Asim Munir and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif as his reasons for holding off on resuming military operations. "I have therefore directed our Military to continue the Blockade and, in all other respects, remain ready and able, and will therefore extend the Ceasefire until such time as their proposal is submitted, and discussions are concluded, one way or the other," Trump wrote.[1][2]

items.title: Iran calls US port blockade an 'act of war' as ceasefire set to expire Wednesday

featured_image.name: Iran war updates: Uncertainty over talks, Trump says deal to come ‘quickly’

items.description: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi declared on Tuesday that the US naval blockade of Iranian ports constitutes an "act of war" and a violation of the fragile ceasefire between Washington and Tehran, as the two-week truce enters its final hours with no extension in sight and the prospect of resumed bombing looming over the region.[1][2]

items.title: Vance trip to Islamabad on hold as Iran ceasefire deadline looms

featured_image.name: Vance has not yet left for Iran talks in Pakistan, source ...

items.description: Diplomatic efforts to end the US-Iran war hit a wall on Tuesday as Vice President JD Vance's planned trip to Islamabad was put on hold and Tehran sent mixed signals about whether it would join a second round of peace talks, raising fears that the fragile two-week ceasefire could collapse without a deal.

items.title: CATL unveils EV battery with 621-mile range, sub-7-minute charge

featured_image.name: CATL launches battery innovations to strengthen global ...

items.description:
CATL on Tuesday launched a suite of battery technologies at its Super Technology Day in Beijing, headlined by a third-generation Qilin battery delivering a 1,000-kilometer (621-mile) driving range and a third-generation Shenxing battery that charges from 10% to 98% in under seven minutes.[1][2][3]

The announcements position the world's largest EV battery maker to extend its market dominance ahead of the Beijing Auto Show, which opens Friday.

items.title: Trump calls seized Iran-bound ship cargo a 'gift from China'

featured_image.name: Seized Iranian cargo ship made multiple stops in China ...

items.description: President Donald Trump on Tuesday described the cargo aboard an Iranian-flagged ship seized by U.S. forces as a "gift from China" to Iran, injecting a new source of friction into the U.S.-China relationship less than a month before a planned presidential summit in Beijing. The comment came as the fragile U.S.-Iran ceasefire nears expiration and investigators continue to examine thousands of containers aboard the vessel.

items.title: Vance's Pakistan trip delayed as Iran ceasefire nears expiration

featured_image.name: Vance's Pakistan trip on hold as Iran refuses to commit to ...

items.description:
Vice President JD Vance did not depart Washington for Pakistan on Tuesday as planned, throwing a second round of U.S.-Iran peace talks into doubt just two days before a fragile ceasefire is set to expire.

Vance was expected to leave Tuesday morning for Islamabad to lead the American delegation in negotiations aimed at ending the conflict with Iran, which began in late February. Instead, he remained at the White House for policy meetings, according to CNN's Alayna Treene. It remains unclear whether the trip will happen at all.[1][2]

items.title: Macron pledges support for Lebanon ahead of Israel talks

featured_image.name: FRANCE-LEBANON-POLITICS-DIPLOMACY

items.description: French President Emmanuel Macron met with Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam at the Élysée Palace on Tuesday, reaffirming France's commitment to the ceasefire in Lebanon and pledging to help strengthen Beirut's position ahead of a second round of direct talks with Israel later this week in Washington.[1][2]

items.title: Trump rejects cease-fire extension as Iran vows ‘no talks under threat’

featured_image.name: Direct U.S.-Iran talks fail to reach resolution after ...

items.description: Iran's chief negotiator Ali Bagheri Kani declared on Tuesday that Iran will not engage in negotiations while facing threats from Western powers, demanding a framework of mutual respect as a precondition for any diplomatic engagement. The statement, delivered during a press conference in Tehran, comes less than 48 hours before the US-Iran ceasefire is set to expire on Wednesday, April 22.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: NATO revives Cold War-era sub hunting as Russia pushes into Arctic

featured_image.name: 35 knots speeding nuclear attack submarine joins Russia's fleet

items.description: As global attention remains fixed on the conflict in the Middle East, a quieter but consequential confrontation is unfolding beneath the waves of the Arctic and North Atlantic. Bloomberg reported on April 21 that NATO is locked in a Cold War-style undersea standoff with Russia, whose advanced nuclear submarines are pushing the alliance to revamp anti-submarine warfare capabilities not seen since the Soviet era.[1][2]

items.title: Dutch intelligence warns Chinese cyberattacks on West will intensify

featured_image.name: Dutch intel agency: Volume, complexity of cyberattacks rises

items.description:
The Dutch military intelligence agency MIVD on Tuesday released its annual report for 2025, warning that the risk of Chinese cyberattacks targeting Western governments and defense industries is growing and expected to intensify further this year.[1][2]

MIVD Director Peter Reesink used the report's release to issue a broader call for European self-reliance in security, saying the rules-based international order that the continent has depended on for decades is under strain. "It is precisely in this space, where rules blur and power becomes more decisive, that threats grow," Reesink said. "Europe must increasingly take responsibility for its own security."[2][1]

items.title: South Korean researchers build 'gas battery' that turns pollution into power

featured_image.name: South Korean scientists build 'gas battery' that turns ...

items.description: Researchers at Sungkyunkwan University in South Korea have developed a novel device they call a "gas battery" that captures greenhouse gases from the atmosphere and simultaneously converts them into electricity — a concept that could reshape how the world thinks about carbon capture.

items.title: Trump says Iran ceasefire extension 'highly unlikely' as deadline looms

featured_image.name: Trump says extension of ceasefire with Iran 'highly unlikely ...

items.description: A two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran is set to expire Wednesday evening, with President Donald Trump declaring it "highly unlikely" he will extend the truce, raising the prospect of a return to hostilities as diplomatic efforts scramble to avert further escalation.

items.title: Russia's oil output drops most in six years after Ukraine drone strikes

featured_image.name: Russia blames Ukraine drone strike for massive blazes at oil ...

items.description: Russia has been forced to slash oil production by 300,000 to 400,000 barrels per day in April compared with first-quarter levels, marking the largest monthly decline in six years, according to Reuters. The drop comes as sustained Ukrainian drone attacks have crippled key export infrastructure across the Baltic and Black Sea, while the halted Druzhba pipeline to Europe compounds a deepening bottleneck in Russian oil logistics.[1][2]

items.title: UNESCO report finds its sites sheltering 60% of mapped species

featured_image.name: UNESCO sites are havens for rare biodiversity under growing ...

items.description: UNESCO-designated sites are serving as critical refuges for biodiversity, supporting the livelihoods of nearly 900 million people, and absorbing a substantial share of the world's carbon emissions, according to the first comprehensive assessment of the global network released on Tuesday, April 21.[1][2]

items.title: US boards second sanctioned Iranian vessel in three days

featured_image.name: US forces board ship in Indian Ocean that fled Caribbean ...

items.description: U.S. forces boarded the oil tanker M/T Tifani in the Indian Ocean on Tuesday, the Pentagon announced, marking the second vessel seized in three days as Washington escalates enforcement of its naval blockade targeting Iran. The boarding came just two days after the dramatic seizure of the Iranian-flagged cargo ship Touska in the Gulf of Oman on Sunday — the first use of force since the blockade began on April 13.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Seized Iranian ship Touska likely carried dual-use cargo, sources say

featured_image.name: Iran war updates: Uncertainty over talks, Trump says deal to come ‘quickly’

items.description: U.S. naval forces attacked and seized the Iranian-flagged cargo ship MV Touska on April 19 after a six-hour standoff in the Gulf of Oman, marking the first such enforcement action since the United States imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports on April 13. Iran condemned the seizure as "maritime piracy" and vowed military retaliation, pulling out of planned peace talks in Pakistan and casting doubt on a fragile ceasefire set to expire on April 21.[1][2]
